resources.string: Air Buzz needs the Nearby devices permission to talk to your Fitbit Air.
Bluetooth is off. Turn it on so Air Buzz can reach the band.
No Fitbit Air paired with this phone. Pair it in the Google Health app first, then come back.
Allow notifications so the alarm can show a Stop button and workouts keep running with the screen off.

Keep the band\'s own alarm on as a backup (set it in Google Health). Air Buzz cannot set the band\'s alarm: it buzzes the band from this phone over Bluetooth, so keep the phone nearby with Bluetooth on.

Wakes you up to that many minutes early, when your heart rate rises at least 8 bpm above your night baseline for 2 minutes (a sign of light sleep). It starts listening 10 minutes before the window to learn the baseline, which uses some extra battery on the band and the phone. Needs \"share heart rate\" on in Google Health.
The band buzzes 20 times, again every 2 minutes, until you tap Stop. If the band cannot be reached twice in a row, the phone rings right away, even with this switch off.
Exact alarms are not allowed for Air Buzz, so the alarm may be late. Allow \"Alarms & reminders\".
For reliable alarms, let Air Buzz run without battery restrictions.
Test alarm set for 1 minute from now. You can lock the phone.
Smart wake: watching your heart rate until %1$s
Smart wake is watching your heart rate
Your band is buzzing. Tap to stop.
Every minute on the minute: one buzz at the start of each minute, 10 rounds.
20 s work, 10 s rest, 8 rounds. The 10 s rests are too short for the wrist, so the phone beeps for them.
Your own work, rest and rounds.
Each %1$s is shorter than %2$d s, too short for the wrist (a buzz takes a few seconds to arrive). The phone will beep for it instead.
Wrist: long fast buzz = work, short slow buzz = rest, very long = done. Buzzes are sent %1$d s early to cover the delay.
Another session is running. Stop it first.
Band did not answer (%1$s). Falling back to the phone.
Enter your age (max HR = 220 − age) or your measured max heart rate.
Z1 50–60 % very easy · Z2 60–70 % easy · Z3 70–80 % moderate · Z4 80–90 % hard · Z5 90–100 % max
Short buzz = below the zone, speed up. Long buzz = above the zone, ease off. After 10 s out of the zone, at most every 45 s. No \"speed up\" buzz in the first minute.
Learn the buzzes before you rely on them. Each one takes a few seconds to reach the band; tap \"I felt it\" when you feel it to measure the delay.
How long a buzz takes to reach your wrist. Usually 3–5 s.
No heart rate? Turn on \"share heart rate\" for the Air in the Google Health app, and wear the band snugly.
Not possible with the Air: setting the band\'s own alarm, detecting taps on the band, and heart-rate variability (the band sends no RR intervals).
